To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cognitive accounts of design can inform design of CAD systems for supporting collaborative, conceptual, creative design and can help assess their use.

cognitive studies of design inform the development of knowledge-based CAD and can be used to assess their use in design practice and provide new insights on human interaction with knowledge based CAD.
the next generation CAD systems will be based on a cognitive account of design, and will support collaborative design and creative design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how cognitive studies of human design can inform the next generation of CAD systems.
the next generation of CAD systems that are cognitive, collaborative, conceptual, creative.
how to develop and deploy knowledge-based CAD systems that can support collaborative, conceptual, creative, and cognitive design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the next generation knowledge-based CAD systems would be characterized by four dimensions: cognitive, collaborative, conceptual, creative.

the four characteristics we envision for the next generation of CAD systems, namely, cognitive, collaborative, conceptual, creative, have been illustrated by our study in biologically Inspired Design, and we believe that the study provides enough promise to justify continued work on knowledgebased CAD systems for biologically inspired Design.

the four characteristics of CAD systems we have identified in this paper are important, and that the study in the design of a knowledge-based system for biologically inspired conceptual design provides an illustration of the usefulness of these characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the next generation CAD systems are not just about the tools, but also about how to use the tools.
the cognitive study of design has a lot to offer to the development and deployment of knowledge-based CAD, and vice versa.

the next generation knowledge-based CAD systems should be based on cognitive theories of design, and that such CAD systems will support collaborative design by enabling designers to work together in the same design environment; conceptual design by providing designers access to a variety of knowledge resources that can help them conceptualize designs; and creative design by providing designers the ability to generate new designs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the next generation CAD systems will be based on the integration of cognitive studies of design with the development of CAD tools for supporting collaborative, conceptual, creative design.
the four dimensions of CAD we have identified are complementary, and together can provide a framework for the next generation of CAD systems.
the development and use of knowledge-based CAD is an important area for cognitive studies of design.
